summary: Backend testing for RCC Leads CRM. 25/25 pytest cases passed covering auth (admin/filler login, /me, wrong-pw 401), user mgmt (admin creates closer, non-admin 403, /users/closers visibility for admin+filler, closer 403), leads CRUD (create with assignment, duplicate phone/instagram_id 409, role-scoped GET, search case-insensitive, follow_up_today filter, update + reassign closer, status PATCH with required follow_up_date, closer-cannot-touch-others-lead 403, role-restricted DELETE) and stats aggregation (admin only, filler 403). All endpoints behaved as specified.

minor.issue: Returns HTTP 200 on creation; convention is 201 Created. Cosmetic, not breaking.

search regex is unescaped — special regex chars in user input could break the query or be exploited for ReDoS. Wrap with re.escape(). Also search only matches instagram_id; spec implies general search but functional req met.
Returns 400; 409 Conflict would be more semantically correct (matches duplicate-lead behavior).
follow_up_date stored as raw string; comparison is string-equality with today's UTC ISO date. If filler enters local-tz date, may miss matches. Acceptable given spec but document timezone assumption.

action_items: (Optional) Use 201 for resource creation endpoints (POST /api/users, POST /api/leads) and 409 for duplicate email on POST /api/users for consistency with duplicate lead behavior.
(Optional) Escape regex in search param: query['instagram_id'] = {'$regex': re.escape(search), '$options': 'i'} to prevent ReDoS and special-char issues.
critical_code_review_comments: FastAPI on_event('startup') is deprecated in newer FastAPI versions; consider lifespan context. Functional today.

CORS uses both allow_origins=['*'] and allow_credentials=True — browsers reject cookies with wildcard origins. Backend works for token auth but cookie-based auth from a different origin will silently fail in the browser. Use allow_origin_regex with explicit origins or set allow_origins to the frontend URL when allow_credentials=True.
Email is normalized to lowercase server-side which is good, but UserPublic model is unused (endpoints return raw dicts). Consider response_model=UserPublic for schema validation.
STATUSES validation only happens in PATCH /status; PUT /leads/{id} doesn't update status — fine, but document that status is only mutable via PATCH endpoint.
_seed_user updates name/role on every restart if password changed — could clobber a renamed admin. Acceptable for fixed-seed admins.
